_comment: Single source of truth for the Aptitude Report — shared with the frontend, which imports
this file directly (same pattern as categories.json). Keep it data-only: the maths lives in
backend/utils/cbatStanine.js and backend/utils/cbatAptitudeReport.js, the wording in
Transcribed from real OASC 'Aptitude Scores' sheets (APPLICATION_INFO/cbat scores). Each
battery is one role. A battery scores a candidate across weighted domains; each domain is fed
by named tests with multipliers. Every test yields a stanine (1-9), a domain's stanine is the
multiplier-weighted mean of its tests, and the battery score is
Pass is score >= cutoff. Domain weights sum to 100 in every battery (asserted in tests).
_minCoverageComment: The score is renormalised over the weight we could actually measure, which is right at 90%
coverage and dangerous at 16%: it turns a sliver of evidence into a confident PASS. A player
who uses the Easier mode wherever it is offered lands at 14-18% on several batteries, because
the heavily weighted tests (CUT and SAT are 49% of Control Officer (ATC) between them) are
exactly the ones with an Easier mode.
Below this much coverage the battery reports status 'provisional': the score is still returned,
but it is not a pass or a fail and no part of the UI may present it as one.

_testsComment: games: which SkyWatch CBAT-style game(s) estimate this test. Empty = SkyWatch has no game for
it yet, so it is excluded from the estimate and reported as an uncovered gap.
match: 'direct'  — our game is a simulation of the same test
'proxy'   — a different game that trains the same underlying skill; flagged in the UI
Where two games are listed the test stanine is the mean of whichever the user has played.
The expansions below are the RAF's own, taken from the test list in the CBAT guide corpus
(APPLICATION_INFO/chat_dumps) rather than guessed from the initials — two of them are not what
the abbreviation suggests. MATF is the Table Reading Test, not a multi-attribute task battery.
TRT is the Target Recognition Test, which is what our Target game simulates; it was briefly
mapped the other way round, so check the corpus before re-reading any code by its initials.
DRT is mapped but unreferenced: none of the 13 transcribed batteries uses it, so it scores
nothing today. It stays because the mapping is confirmed and a battery transcribed later will
pick it up for free. Our Symbols game is the glossary's Visual Search Test, which carries no
code at all on any sheet seen so far — hence no entry for it.
OPEN QUESTION: VISS sits in the Perceptual domain, which fits the Visual Search Test (Symbols)
better than it fits Visualisation (a spatial task). It is mapped to Visualisation on the
strength of the name alone. Only WSOP (ISR) uses it, at about 7% of that battery.
SMA was the single largest uncovered weight left after those five: it is 15% of the Pilot battery
and 12% of Pilot ISR (RPAS), sharing the Psychomotor domain with RTT, so every Pilot report was
renormalising over a missing seventh of its evidence. Our game is a 'direct' match on the
mechanic — the same compensatory tracking of a drifting dot against a fixed crosshair — but not on
the apparatus: the real test splits the axes across a joystick and foot pedals and ours puts both
on one control. That affects how hard it is to fly, not what it measures.
SIT / SLT / VLT / MATF / VIG1 were all uncovered gaps until the games behind them were built.
They are not marginal: MATF and SIT both carry weight in the Pilot battery, and SLT sits in
its Symbolic Reasoning domain alongside ANT. VGIL_SPEED is a 'proxy' rather than a 'direct'
on purpose — it is a separate SPEED sub-score of the same Vigilance test, and our game reports
one accumulating score that conflates speed with accuracy, so it estimates that sub-score
rather than simulating it.
Their anchors are the only ones in this file NOT sourced from production play — there is none
yet. They come from the demo bands in utils/cbatFakeLeaderboard.js, which is where every other
game's anchors started too. Requery and retune once these have real runs behind them.
_anchorsComment: Two points per game turn a raw SkyWatch score into a stanine: `median` is the score of a
middling player (stanine 5, the centre of the curve) and `strong` is a clearly good run
(stanine 8). Everything else is linear from those two — see utils/cbatStanine.js.
MEASURED (2026-09-06) by scripts/calibrateStanineAnchors.js. Both anchors are quantiles of
one value per player — the mean of their last 3 runs, which is exactly the estimator the
report scores a user on (FORM_WINDOW in utils/cbatAptitudeReport.js). The stanine band table
in utils/cbatStanine.js sets the targets: stanine 5 spans P40-P60 and stanine 8 spans
P89-P96, so the band centres are median = P50 and strong = P92.5.
Measure it the same way if you retune. The previous anchors did not: `median` was a typical
SINGLE run and `strong` was never measured at all — it was the demo ceiling from
utils/cbatFakeLeaderboard.js, a number chosen to make fake leaderboard rows look plausible.
Comparing a 3-run mean against single-run spread squeezes every stanine toward 5, because
averaging strips out within-player noise. More data does not fix that; it repeats it.
One value PER PLAYER, never per run: a run-level quantile is dominated by heavy users, and
heavy users are the practised ones, so it drifts upward on volume alone.
These are SkyWatch's own norms, not the RAF's — see the disclaimer the report page carries.
More players makes them a better description of OUR field; it does not close the gap to the
RAF's applicant distribution, so the disclaimer stays however good the sample gets.
Re-run the script every 6-12 months rather than continuously. Re-anchoring to a rising median
norms away improvement: players practise, the median climbs, and someone who genuinely got
better sees a flat stanine. That is tolerable at this cadence because the raw-score sparkline
already shows progress in absolute terms — stanine is standing, sparkline is improvement.
PROVISIONAL — under the script's 100-player cohort gate, so the exact values are imprecise:
`rtt` (50 players), `cut` (63), `sat` (62), `vigilance` (33), `matf` (35). They were updated
anyway because they were not slightly off, they were broken: an average player was scoring
stanine 9 on rtt/cut/vigilance and stanine 1 on sat. Re-run the script once each clears 100.
HELD, still on demo-tuned values and mildly inflated at the top end — `dad` (91 players,
strong sits at P97), `visualisation-2d` (86, P100), `trace-2` (78, P100), `dpt-hard` (66,
`vlt` (8, P63). An average player still reads 5-6 on these, so they can wait for a cohort.
`slt`, `vlt` and `trace-2` may never be quantifiable: their scores are small integers, so
P50 and P92.5 collide and the step degenerates. Those keep hand-judged anchors.

batteries.label: Pilot
batteries.note: This is the toughest role to get. Its pass mark is 22 points higher than any Control role.

batteries.label: Control Officer (ATC)
batteries.note: Almost half of this role rides on Strategic Task Management, so CUT and SAT matter most.

batteries.label: Non-Commissioned Control (ATC)
batteries.note: Same tests as Control Officer (ATC), but with the lowest pass mark of any role.
